newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco stocks end higher on bank merger.
newsitem.headline: Morocco stocks end higher on bank merger.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended the week on Friday higher, lifted mainly by confirmation of a bank takeover and by trading in the market's largest capitalisations, a market analyst said.
The all-share index closed at 437.86 points, up from 435.65 points last week.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, gained one dirham over one week to close at 500 dirhams.
ONA has diversified stakes in more than 100 companies and a capitalisation of more than 8.3 billion dirhams.

"The bourse consolidated its upward trend this week due largely to active trading in the blue chip firms and banking sector. It was also marked by the announcement of the Wafaban-Uniban merger," a Casablanca-based broker said.
Wafabank confirmed this week market rumours of its purchase of Spanish Uniban bank.
A Wafabank official said the final agreement would be sealed when Uniban's general assembly meets on December 30 and after approval by the monetary authorities.
Wafabank, a liquid stock, jumped to 551 dirhams from 522 dirhams a week earlier.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, remained stable at 685 dirhams, traders said.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, gained eight dirhams to close at 315 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 19.6 million dirhams against 43.8 million dirhams last Friday.
